title: Deep dust dimming of field dwarfs occurs with extreme warm dust: the old dimmer Gaia DR3 4466400095283726080 emits 3.6 percent of its light at 400 K, and its 3-5 um flux rose after its 2021 dips
abstract: Prior campaign studies found rare, deep, aperiodic dust dips on field dwarfs and a 4.6 um excess on some of them. We tested what the dust of the new dimmer Gaia DR3 4466400095283726080 (G4466) is, and whether dimming and strong warm dust occur together in an all-sky sample. G4466 has W3 and W4 excesses of 12 and 29 times the photosphere (confirmed by Legacy Surveys forced photometry): one 400 K blackbody with L_dust/L_star = 3.6 percent. Its Gaia radial velocity gives a space velocity of 86 km/s, so the star is probably older than 1 Gyr. Pan-STARRS1, Gaia and ZTF show dips since at least 2010, to 0.8 mag. Relative to 38 field stars, NEOWISE W1 and W2 became brighter by 0.092 +- 0.005 and 0.152 +- 0.008 mag between the 2022 February and August visits, after the 2021 dips; the added flux is about 1050 K hot dust with 0.7 percent of L_star. SPHEREx (456 images, 2025-2026) shows the 4.1-5.0 um flux 0.22 +- 0.02 mag above the pre-2022 level, an 800 K excess for the preferred template (570 K for the Gaia colour), and no 3.1 um ice band in the quiet state (depth < 0.028). The M dwarf dimmer Gaia DR3 3768075658908734720 also has a 10 times W3 excess (about 6 percent). In 951 Gaia DR3 dwarfs at |b| > 20 deg with a confirmed 12 um excess (5e-5 of field dwarfs), ZTF shows 3 dust dimmers of 612 against 0 of 1,174 matched controls (p = 0.04), including the new dimmer Gaia DR3 2874265305022213760 (230 K, 3 percent). Without the two known stars the forward test is 1 of 610 (p = 0.34). Of five variability-selected dimmers with G < 17, one has a confirmed excess where 7e-5 is expected. Thus deep dimming of field dwarfs goes with extreme-debris-disc-level warm dust, and in G4466 the dust production changed within months. Limitations: no spectra, template-dependent temperatures, few dimmers, possible galaxy blends, an a posteriori choice of the W3 test.
